title: Roster Management
text:
EC (Executive Council) meetings are when the Exec. officers and all advisers meet. This needs to happen at least once a month, but you don’t need to worry about scheduling it yourself.
EC meetings are different from OB (Officer Board) meetings, which are only the collegiate members on Exec meetings without advisers. 

To prepare for EC meetings you need to prepare 2 things: 

Meeting Agenda
Meeting Minutes


To prepare for OB meetings you still need to send Exec the meeting agenda, but you don’t need to send it to the advisers or take minutes. I recommend taking minutes anyways, but that is just me. You can only submit minutes from EC meetings, so if you do take OB minutes, make sure you know which minutes are which.


The meeting agenda will need to be sent in the Exec group chat early (ish) on Sunday Morning. The timing doesn’t need to be exactly the same every week, but time it so there are a couple hours before that week’s meeting to have it filled out. 
Around 1 hour before the meeting is planned to start, check the meeting agenda again. It more than likely was not filled out by every officer. Send a reminder text to the Exec group chat so people remember to fill it out. 
Around 30 minutes before the EC zoom, send the filled out (either entirely or mostly) agenda to the adviser group chat. 



The meeting minutes are important, as they are submitted to IHQ. There needs to be a copy of the meeting minutes for each month of the academic year submitted to them. Before the EC meetings, you can edit simple things like date/time with the template. During EC, you need to update the attendance and take minutes. For attendance, I just look at the names in the zoom. For minutes, update them with the level of information you believe is appropriate. 
I recommend keeping minutes for OB as well, as it is easier to remember to take them every meeting rather than keeping track of OB vs EC, but it is up to you!
You don’t need to send the minutes to anyone until you submit them to IHQ by the deadline. 
The deadline for submitting minutes is around the deadline for submitting good standing points, which varies year to year. It is often around the end of the academic semester, so in early December and late April. You can submit minutes every month, if it is easier to do so. You can also upload them all on the same day if that is best for you. 
Before or during EC/OB Meetings, you will have a copy of the slides to fill out for that day’s chapter (assuming you are attending a regular meeting on Sunday). Fill out your slide, but also ensure that you upload the most accurate flare QR code.

title: Change in Membership Status
text:
Change in Membership Status is when someone wants to change their membership in the chapter. The default status is “Initiate” when the member is initiated or “New Member” if they haven’t been initiated. Most CIMS cases deal with the OFFICIAL roster in MyAlphaGam, although each has its own rules as outlined in the CIMS Manual.
There are multiple statuses that a member can change to:
There are more statuses, as seen in the CIMS manual . The ones above are the most common.
Review the manual for more details on these statuses:

title: Change in Membership Status
text:
Alumna Status
Alumna is often used when people graduate from the chapter. There are some instances where people can go on an “emergency alumna” when they are away from school.
What to know about Alumna: 

It is called Alumnae in the handbooks so that’s what you need to search if you control F
Seniors are alumna after graduation
Alumna for graduation and emergency purposes is executed on Admin’s end in MyAlphaGam

Go to the roster
Find the person’s name
Click the three dots at the end of their name tile
Click “Update Contact’s Status”
Click the drop down (“Select Status”) > select “Alumna”

The process for changing a member to an Alumna is the same process for changing them to other statuses as well, as seen in the “Select Status” drop-down on the “Update Contact’s Status” page

title: Change in Membership Status
text:
Terminated and Withdrawn Status
Terminated is often used when New Members choose to leave the chapter before they’re initiated. 

Withdrawn is used when Initiates choose to leave the chapter, any time after they’re initiated. 
Withdrawn and Terminated (Voluntary)  members must choose to leave the chapter on their own through MyAlphaGam. 

Here is a rough script of what I say
In order to be removed from the roster: 

The member must fill out the original form
The member must reaffirm their decision. I think this form is sent in an email but done in MyAlphaGam although I am not 100% sure

People always told me they received an automated email roughly 72 hours after the first time they submitted the CIMS form

They must pay all of the amount that is on their BillHighway (Ask VP Finance for this)
Confirm with VP Finance that they are good to be removed, and with the President (just so they’re aware)… once that is all good hit “Submit Chapter Confirmation” button, fill out required information

EC doesn’t meet to discuss withdrawals just pick the date that you are confirming their withdrawal on 


When someone reaches out to you about withdrawing OR they withdraw without reaching out to you first: 

Ensure you reach out to them, see what their reasoning is for wanting to withdraw

Sometimes they leave a comment that you can read on their CIMS request in MyAlphaGam




Offer to meet with them to talk anything through
Have VP Membership and/or VP Wellness meet with them / reach out to them
Inform them of options: 

If time is a concern: Inactive Status
If money is a concern: Meeting with the Finance Advisor and VP Finance 
Long term emergency circumstances: emergency alumna
If there is an extenuating circumstance, loop Pres. and Admin Advisor in

title: Inactive Status
text:
There is also Inactive Status, which is part of the CIMS Manual but is different from the other statuses where you are changing the official chapter roster. Inactive status is a special status that members can apply for if they are unable to be a full member of the chapter. Examples include working full time/school, taking more credits, not enough time, etc. There are many reasons why someone may go inactive. 

Important things about inactive: 

People may only go inactive for ONE semester

It is an option to go inactive for more semesters but it is in rare circumstances only 

People still have to go to RTS/Recruitment
They have to pay for merch if they want it 
They have to pay for date night and formal if they choose to attend
They have (slightly) decreased dues
EC must meet in order to vote to let someone be inactive

You will send inactive paper work in advance, present their case to EC, and vote

Our chapter is just under 200 members as of now, this includes active, inactive, and abroad members 

This means that the TOTAL number of inactive cases you can have in a given semester is no more than 10 
Once we get more new members, this number may change, and then may change again when the seniors graduate, see the CIMS manual


Inactive Paperwork: [There is a PDF you need to send] This is what you will send to anyone wanting to go inactive. I suggest sending it over email as that is the chapter’s admin email and is 

Taken more seriously 
Better for keeping track of important, potentially confidential paperwork.

The document, and many other templates and documents you might need are in the Appendix of the CIMS manual. 

Here is an example template of the email that I send when I reach out to people with inactive status paperwork:
Once they are approved/denied for inactive status you need to inform them of this change as soon as you can. There are templates in the CIMS manual, but I prefer to write in my own tone.
Once inactive, all you need to do for the member to be officially inactive is to update YOUR roster(s) with their new status and store their paperwork in an organized folder on the google drive, there is nothing to do in MyAlphaGam or with IHQ
More inactive status info: CIMS Manual

title: Inactive Email Example
text:
Here is an example template of the email that I send when I reach out to people with inactive status paperwork:
Hi {NAME}
I have attached the pdf that you need to fill out and send back to me in order to go inactive. I also ask that you write me a short paragraph describing your reasoning for wanting to do so. Sometimes the formatting can get screwed up on the PDF, feel free to send the paragraph in the body of the email that you attach the document to.
This will be read aloud at the next EC meeting before we vote on your status. It is not a guarantee that you will be approved to go inactive, but the information shared during the voting process will remain confidential.
A few reminders:

Inactive status is not retroactive, you must continue to attend any mandatory events until your status is officially confirmed by EC
If you are recruiting next semester you must attend RTS

If you haven’t recruited before you must attend all RTS sessions, including MC ’25 sessions
If you have recruited before, you only need to attend RTS sessions that are held for all recruiters

You are still responsible for paying dues on time throughout the year
If approved, your inactive dues will not cover date night(s) or formal, if you choose to go you will have to pay for these separately
Inactive status is only for the rest of the fall semester and is only being granted for the Fall 2025 semester

The next meeting of EC will be on Sunday, September 28th. Please do your best to get these papers to me by tonight. Feel free to text me if you have any questions or concerns!
Best,
{Name}
^I recommend that you change the template to suit you/your tone.

title: Directors & Newsletter
text:
You will have 2 directors:

Director of Communications 
Director of Attendance 

This is not the official name, you can have them do whatever you need them to do, attendance just happens to be a big job I needed help with
Our chapter doesn’t use the “Director of Chapter History” as directed in the Administration Team Handbook, this director is replacing that

The reason why we don’t have the director of chapter history is most likely because our chapter recently made the jump from structure C to D in the past couple of years– feel free to explore these responsibilities if you want to include more in your position!





The biggest thing that the director of communications does is the newsletter, see below. For the official responsibilities of this director, see the Director of Communication information in the Admin Team Handbook. This is where you can also check the Director of History responsibilities, if you’re interested. 



Like briefly stated above, the director of attendance is an extra director awarded to VP Admin in Spring 2025. You can make this position your own based on your needs! 
I recommend:

Having them help with attendance records (moving stuff from flare > google drive/sheets) 
Having them help with excuses 

This really depends on who your director is, excuses can be personal and must be handed with privacy 

Having them help do attendance, especially if you can’t make an event
For normal events, just give them the QR code
For recruitment, since I recommend doing manual attendance, you can tell them to bring their computer too to help with the process!

title: Bylaws: Excuses Outlined
text:
As per pages 8 & 9 of our bylaws:
“Excused Absence

An absence may be excused by the Executive Council for a valid reason.
An absence shall be explained to the Executive Council, in writing, via the Vice President–Administration at least three days prior to the event.
Valid reasons for excused absences shall be:

Serious illness or death in the immediate family
Serious illness of the member or new member
Representing the college or university officially
Meetings, examinations or interviews for future secondary programs of study with the confirmation of supporting documentation
Future employment/internship interview(s) with the confirmation of supporting documentation
Previously contracted employment that cannot be rescheduled
Study excuse: Two excuses shall be allowed per academic term. Study excuses may only be used for chapter and/or new member meetings for study purposes.
Personal absence: One personal absence shall be allowed per academic term.

A personal absence may only be used for a required Fraternity event or required chapter event.

A personal absence must be for a legitimate reason and approved by the Excuse Note Committee or Executive Council.”




For more information see Alpha Chapter Bylaws 2025

title: Roster Management
text:
There are a couple rosters that will be helpful to maintain. The most important roster is the official one that is found in MyAlphaGam. This will be updated automatically after CIMS cases, although it can take a couple days. The only other time you need to update it is when there are different status changes as outlined in the Change in Membership Status section. 
You can use the MyAlphaGam roster as the most accurate and updated roster of the whole chapter (UNLESS you just had a CIMS case, in which that person may still be listed). It is exportable to excel, which is where I do any editing (such as parsing first and last names, reordering) before I copy and paste into google sheet.

I recommend keeping the following rosters: 

General Roster

Actives page
Inactive page
Abroad page
Totals on all pages

Actives only roster
Roster with all members and their MCs
Attendance roster: up to you how you do attendance records! For more see the attendance section


You might also want a roster with only seniors, and/or a roster with the classes of everyone. 

At the end of the day, it is up to you which rosters you keep, but the above was what was helpful to me, especially when another EC member had a question related to our roster(s).

You must keep the relevant information, regardless of how you choose to track it: 

Peoples statuses (inactive vs. active vs. abroad)
Attendance Records

title: Miscellaneous
text:
You need to have at least one non mandatory sisterhood event a semester. There is currently $75 budgeted towards this. You can use that money for more than one event, or you can spend it all on one bigger event. 
The budget is reset in May, so spend all of your money before then. In the Fall, your budget is split between your fall and your incoming officer’s budget. 
You can come up with whatever event ideas you want! If you want to buy anything, you will need to fill out a PRV so the VP Finance can order the items for you. Reach out to VP Finance with more questions regarding this kind of stuff.

title: Excuses & Attendance Records
text:
The way that you approve/deny excuses and keep attendance records is ultimately up to you and your EC. 
For excuse forms, I recommend: 

Sending them out roughly 2 weeks in advance of the event
Making them due roughly 1 week in advance of the event 
Posting the excusals 3-7 days before the event

I usually do 2 or 3 days so people have time to text me 


If the excuse form is for someone else’s event, i.e. Philanthropy, I always sent it to them to have them review it before sending it to the chapter. This is OPTIONAL, I personally did this because I want to have someone else double check the date and time! 

You can format the excuse forms however you want/what works best for approving/denying excuses easily.  
What I recommend: 

I find having the information on one page and the questions on the next is the best way to have people read the information they would otherwise skip
Having first and last name as two different questions so you can do alphabetical order for either 
Having intentional options for members to select in terms of excuses (ie. “work” and “school”) 

best for having a minimal number of invalid excuses submitted 

Having the option to submit multiple photos for proof 

Here is an example excuse form that I have based all my forms off of:  Example Excuse Form
The types of excuses that are allowed are based on the type of event. More important events require stricter excuses. Review the Alpha Chapter Accountability doc for more details. 
Do your best to follow the Bylaws as closely as you can. This ensures that excusals are uniform and fair across members, events, and reasons people are requesting to be excused. 


Ensure that you notify members of the deadlines for the excuses multiple ways. There is always someone that doesn’t listen and they will tell you that they didn’t know the form was due when it was. If you have various methods of communication, then you can tell that person that their late excuse isn’t valid with a more concrete explanation. 


What I recommend: 

Announcing at Chapter when you post the form
Announcing at Chapter when the form is due
Posting the excuse form in the same place every time (I do the chapter resource doc for easy access)
Posting the deadline under the link to the excuse form 
Announcing in Flare when you post the form
Announcing in Flare when the form is due 
Making a flare calendar event when the form is due

with a link to the form 
When the form is due 
A reminder notification that goes off 10 minutes before it is due

title: Excuses & Attendance Records
text:
Attendance Records
Ensure you keep records in writing, this way if there are any issues there is “proof.” It is up to you how to keep Attendance Records, however, according to my Spring 2025 feedback form, people preferred to have one large sheet/ Attendance Tracker rather than smaller sheets for each event. 

The way that you do attendance is different depending on the event. Review this fine outline to see how different events are fined. 

My recommendations: 

Recruitment: you stand at the door for check in and check out to ensure that everyone
is physically there. This is the chapter’s MOST IMPORTANT event so although it is tedious I think this is important

Recruitment is fined per party but you don’t need to worry about this, recruitment will very clearly know who is at each party 
You will be working with someone from the recruitment team to do excuses and attendance… more to come

New Mem Events: Have one of the VPNME Directors do this
Random events (such as Panhel required events, philanthropy, etc.) have one of the Exec members going do attendance via flare
Most Events (Chapter, big/little, OUR philanthropy, etc.) use a flare QR code, opt in to do check in and check out if it is a really hefty fine / important event (our philanthropy)
Some events need hourly fines (retreat) it is up to you how you do attendance, I would do whatever is easiest
OPTIONAL: Alternative Attendance Form in case flare doesn’t work out

There would be times peoples phone was dead/broken and they needed to checkout, I gave them my phone or had them borrow a friends
Much more reliable than someone coming up to you after something and you having to remember (especially if you forget and then they get fined and then there is no way to actually prove they were there!



VP Finance will need to be able to easily access your attendance in order to give fines to people. Ensure that it is clear if someone was absent for this reason.
